question: An architect is building an agent that must read internal wiki pages, query a ticketing database, and post replies to a chat tool. The team wants to avoid writing and maintaining custom tool-execution code for each integration and wants the agent to autonomously decide when to call each system. Which architecture choice best satisfies this?
options: A) Embed the wiki, database, and chat contents directly into the system prompt on every request so no runtime tool calls are needed
B) Implement a manual tool loop with the Client SDK where application code inspects stop_reason and dispatches hand-written handlers
C) Precompute a static decision tree mapping every possible request to a fixed sequence of API calls the application runs without the model
D) Connect the agent to MCP servers for the wiki, database, and chat tool so each system is exposed through one standardized protocol
correct_answers: D) Connect the agent to MCP servers for the wiki, database, and chat tool so each system is exposed through one standardized protocol
explanations: Incorrect. Embedding all wiki, database, and chat content in every prompt does not scale, quickly exceeds practical context limits, and cannot perform live actions like posting a reply.
Incorrect. A manual Client SDK tool loop requires the team to implement and maintain the tool-execution logic themselves, which is exactly the maintenance burden they want to avoid.
Incorrect. A static decision tree removes the model's autonomous judgment about when to call each system, contradicting the requirement that the agent decide dynamically.

Correct. MCP is the standardized protocol for connecting an AI application to external data sources and tools such as wikis, databases, and chat apps, letting the agent discover and call them without bespoke integration code for each system.
